page: UpCloud STARTER-4xCPU-16GB is a general-purpose virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz with a shared CPU allocation. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 50 GB of local SSD storage alongside one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and single-threaded gzip compression scoring in the top 25%. However, multi-core and memory performance show some limitations. While multi-core stress-ng and Geekbench scores sit in the average range, the large-block read-only memory bandwidth is poor at 6.32 GB/sec, placing it in the bottom 10%. Additionally, Passmark memory and physics tests, along with multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, fall into the bottom 25%, reflecting the shared CPU allocation and memory throughput constraints under heavy, uncached workloads.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this server offers a balanced resource density for budget-conscious deployments, leveraging shared AMD EPYC hardware to deliver capable compute resources without the premium of dedicated cores. It is well-suited for general-purpose workloads such as static web serving, Redis key-value caching, and basic database operations. It is less optimal for memory-intensive applications, large-scale multi-threaded decompression, or complex LLM inference tasks due to its memory bandwidth and shared CPU constraints.
